hook_text: Twenty years ago, this forest was bare sand.
clip_script: Near Richards Bay, KwaZulu-Natal. A dune forest full of trees, birds and monkeys. But it was once bare sand, mined for minerals. Mining clears plants, and animals lose their homes. It leaves waste: rock dumps, and tailings in tailings dams that can burst if badly built. But there's another way. Keep the topsoil, put the sand back, spread the soil, plant indigenous plants. Rehabilitation. And by law, mines must pay for it.
visual_style: Whiteboard bare sand dunes slowly filling with plants, trees and animals, with a side scene of waste rock and a tailings dam.
mood: Hopeful and thoughtful, like watching nature heal.
pacing: Starts with the forest, rewinds to the damage, then shows the healing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find out if there is a rehabilitated mine near you.
